Vocals: Bhai Mohinder Jeet Singh. Poetry: Baba Farid. All credit to the artist.

#punjabi #punjabipoetry #پنجابی #پنجابی_شاعری #poetry

gists: Farid, repay evil with good; do not let anger take hold of your heart.
Then no sickness will touch your body, and you will gain everything.
Farid, those who strike you with their fists, do not strike them back. Go to your own home, and kiss their feet.

Vocals: Hamid Ali Bela. Poetry: Shah Hussain. All credit to the artist.

#punjabi #punjabipoetry #پنجابی #پنجابی_شاعری #poetry

gists: Mother, whom do I tell the pain of separation? My master’s love smoulders in me like a fire; stir it, and the embers glow red.
Sorrow is my bread, thorns are my curry, and my sighs are the firewood I burn.
Says humble faqir Hussain: if I meet my Beloved, I will bloom with joy.

posts.caption:
For someone who is far away. 🤍
Mian Muhammad Bakhsh

#MianMuhammadBakhsh #PunjabiPoetry #پنجابی_شاعری
posts.note: score-only reel; replaced by the lyric-reel format (2026-11-16)

gists: Hold the one point and drop the reckoning; clear away doubt and dread, and make the heart clean. It all comes down to one point.
You rub your forehead on the ground and show off a long prayer niche, yet the meaning never reaches your heart. Can truth stay hidden?
Many came home as pilgrims in fine blue robes, then sold their Hajj for coins. Who could admire that? Can truth stay hidden?
Some go off to the wilds and live on one grain a day, wearing out their bodies for nothing. Life runs out in such retreats.
Hold to the guide, be lost in carefree rapture, want nothing, and keep the heart clean. Bulleh, when was truth ever held back?

gists: Without my beloved, the nights have grown long.
My flesh has wasted away to a bare frame, and my bones rattle.
Love will not stay hidden, however I hide it; separation has pitched its tents in me.
Ranjha is a jogi and I am his jogan; again and again they call me mad.
Says Hussain, the Lord's faqir: I have taken hold of the hem of Your robe.

posts.note: Ratan Singh sings all 5 verses unaccompanied: no instruments and no wordless passage anywhere in the track, so the closing card runs over a quiet breath gap instead of instrumental music. gists: It never sleeps, it only weeps: the body that carries the ache of pain is the one that weeps.
On the maiden's bed, no one has ever slept in comfort.
All four corners of my shawl are sunk in mud; who will wash them clean?
The cure for pain lives inside you; only a saintly healer can bring you to it.
Says Hussain, God's faqir: whatever is written is what comes to pass.
